per_claim.source_quote: The ordering in section [sec:pairtype] is the one nearest-neighbour thermodynamics predicts. This subsection asks whether it is that prediction. The mediator is Definition [def:dg]: the free energy the model itself assigns to the individual pair. Every program in the corpus optimises a sum of such terms, so holding this quantity fixed holds fixed what the design loop was told about the pair. Stratification, and the overlap it needs. $Delta G_{loc}$ is cut at fixed quantiles of the pooled distribution -- $5$ bins, edges fixed once, before any contrast -- and the bin index joins $(design,depth,crossed)$ in the stratum. Because the edges do not depend on the labels, permuting labels cannot rebuild the matched set, which is what Prop. [prop:null] requires. Overlap is real but not free (Fig. [fig:energy], left): G--C pairs average $-4.592$kcal/mol against $-3.002$ for A--U and $-1.859$ for G--U, and the most stable bin holds $776/871/392/584/438$ G--C pairs against $0/73/436/258/349$ A--U ones by bin. per_claim.source_quote: Two facts about the corpus set the scale for everything below, and neither is a test. Where the variance is. Decomposing the design score gives $28.8%$ between targets, $24.1%$ between methods within target, and $47.1%$ within cell, of which $15.1%$ is measurement noise. This is an identity, not a hypothesis, and it is why every estimator in this paper is computed after centring within $(target,method)$: the first two layers are removed by construction rather than adjusted for. How much of the within-cell variance is reproducible at all. The release contains $557$ groups of repeated measurements covering $1983$ rows. This is the one interval in the paper that resamples something other than targets: its unit of replication is the repeated measurement group, as section [sec:preregprotocol] notes.
